## Diagnosis

- **C-13** (blocker): r5's finding is narrowed, not closed. The corrected check is sound only for a worker who names the binding variable `stamper`, and it never verifies that name. Under any other name the union pattern collapses back to the literal path, the invocation set becomes the single variable-assignment line again, and r5's artifact H — a real section whose invocations are all appended after the fixture-guard comparison, which is this clause's own named failing example — prints `inside the guard`. The pin is now the whole load-bearing structure of a blocker check, and it is enforced by prose alone.
  evidence: constitution.md:462-464 `calls=$(/usr/bin/grep -nE 'stamp-confirmed\.sh|\$\{?stamper\}?' ...)` and :468 `[ "$ban" -lt "$first" ] && [ "$last" -lt "$cmp" ]`. Rebuilt r5's five artifacts against the real 1309-line suite (C-17's wiring require_text inserted beside the `scripts/lint-scope.sh` one at :300 in every one) and confirmed the three readings the orchestrator reported: (B) banner, binding and invocations all inside -> 'snap=587 banner=1297 first-call=1298 last-call=1307 cmp=1313' -> **inside the guard**. (F) binding beside `migrator=` at :588 -> 'banner=1298 first-call=591' -> **OUTSIDE THE GUARD**, now a true FAIL since the clause pins the binding inside the section. (H) banner and binding inside, real `bash "$stamper"` lines appended after the comparison -> 'first-call=1298 last-call=1323 cmp=1303' -> **OUTSIDE THE GUARD**, r5's false PASS closed. Also (D) guard message reworded to name the script by filename -> inside; (G) message reworded to 'a migration or stamping test' -> inside; shipped tree -> OUTSIDE on the empty banner. All five readings correct. Then attacked the pin. (M) artifact B verbatim with the binding named `scs` instead of `stamper`, house-style preamble and a real `bash "$scs"` invocation, everything inside the guard: 'snap=587 banner=1297 first-call=1298 last-call=1298 cmp=1314' -> **inside the guard**, but first and last are both line 1298, the assignment. No invocation was measured, and nothing told the worker the pin was broken. (N) r5's artifact H with the binding named `scs` — banner and binding inside, every real invocation appended after the comparison: 'first-call=1298 last-call=1298 cmp=1303' -> **inside the guard**. That is a false PASS on the clause's own failing example at :514, 'a real section, correctly written, appended at :1310 where the fixture guard cannot see it', reproduced under the corrected check. (O) the same artifact with the pinned name -> OUTSIDE, so the only difference between a caught defect and an uncaught one is the worker's choice of identifier. (I) banner and binding inside, section body is two `require_text` calls against SKILL.md and no invocation at all — this clause's first failing example at :514: -> **inside the guard**, because the binding alone satisfies both bounds. Prescribed fix verified against all ten artifacts, below.
- **C-13-FIX** (blocker): The prescribed replacement for C-13's placement block, verified against all ten artifacts with zero regressions. Separate the binding (found by the pinned name) from the uses (found by the variable), and require both to exist and both to sit in bounds. Then a worker who renames the variable gets a true FAIL with an accurate diagnosis instead of a silent pass, and the binding line can no longer stand in for an invocation.
  evidence: Replace constitution.md:459-469 with: `bind=$(/usr/bin/grep -n '^stamper=.*stamp-confirmed\.sh' tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh | cut -d: -f1)` ; `uses=$(/usr/bin/grep -nE '\$\{?stamper\}?' tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh | /usr/bin/grep -v 'require_text' | /usr/bin/grep -v '^[0-9]*:#' | /usr/bin/grep -v 'echo ' | cut -d: -f1)` ; `first=$(printf '%s\n' "$uses" | sort -n | head -1)` ; `last=$(printf '%s\n' "$uses" | sort -n | tail -1)` ; `echo "snap=$snap banner=$ban bind=$bind first-use=$first last-use=$last cmp=$cmp"` ; `[ -n "$ban" ] && [ -n "$bind" ] && [ -n "$first" ] && [ "$snap" -lt "$ban" ] && [ "$ban" -lt "$bind" ] && [ "$bind" -le "$first" ] && [ "$last" -lt "$cmp" ] && echo "inside the guard" || echo "OUTSIDE THE GUARD"`. Add one sentence to the pass conditions: an empty `$bind` or an empty `$uses` is a FAIL, not a pass — the first means the section did not bind under the pinned name, the second means no invocation went through it, and both are the defects the bounds exist to catch. Verified side by side against the shipped r6 block on ten artifacts: agreement on every correct artifact (B, D, G, P -> inside the guard) and on every true failure (F, H, O, and the shipped tree -> OUTSIDE); three false PASSes closed (I, M, N -> OUTSIDE). Artifact P is the braces form `${stamper}`, confirming the widened pattern still matches it. No artifact regressed from a pass to a fail.
- **SHIPPABILITY** (major): The decision the orchestrator asked for. Everything in this document except one code block in C-13 is verified shippable, and no other finding should hold Phase 1. But a worker would not trip over the C-13 defect — nobody trips, the check just goes green — and that is exactly why it cannot be recorded as a minor and passed.
  evidence: What a worker actually meets: eighteen clauses whose checks I ran against a conforming implementation and against adversarial variants, and which discriminate. The script contract is good enough that I transcribed it into a working stamper in one pass. The six carried minors are all real but none of them would block or mislead a worker mid-build — they cost a rework cycle at worst, and several (C-4's scoping, the BASELINE count, the revision marker) cost nothing at all. On the other side: C-13 is the only clause carrying AC7, its placement bound is the only enforcement of a blocker-grade requirement, and it green-lights its own named failing example whenever the binding is not named `stamper`. The two conditions that produce that outcome are not independent — a worker who did not absorb the binding convention in C-13's placement paragraph is the same worker who did not absorb where the section goes, since both live in that paragraph. The fix is one code block plus one sentence, it is written out above, and it is verified. r7 should be an accept-the-fix round: re-run the ten-artifact table, confirm nothing else moved, and pass. Six rounds is expensive and the orchestrator is right that the marginal finding is worth less each time — which is the argument for closing this one properly now rather than carrying a known hole into a build.

The clause text makes the pin visible to a careful reader and missable to a skimmer.
